texts: moth, lamp, devotion
Whenever my mother prays she gets lost completely, like a moth to a lamp, and the house goes silent around her.
doha about a moth & lamp as a picture of loving God
Moth to lamp, soul to its Lord, burning gladly in the only love that is real.
Write a doha about a moth that surrenders itself to the lamp without a second thought, a picture of a devotee who gives up everything for love of God, seeking not reward but only union with him.
Compose a doha about the moth that never asks whether the end is worth it but flies to what it loves, showing how true devotion gives everything and wants nothing in return.
My aunt left everything to take care of a sick stranger, with this strange smile like a moth who has found what it was looking for.
The moth knows no hesitation, no bargaining, only the one love that is bigger than itself.
doha: moth shows what real devotion is like
moth, love of God
My grandmother sits under the old tree each dawn, doesn't say a thing, and says she's meeting the One who never left.
Under the tree the seeker sits, and finds the Beloved was never anywhere else.
Write a doha about a devotee who sits beneath a tree in silence and discovers that God is not found in any faraway place but has been waiting inside his own heart all along.
doha: sitting under a tree and finding god inside
tree, God within
tree, inner devotion
doha abt a tree that grows from a tiny seed like real devotion in the heart

Compose a doha about devotion growing quietly inside the heart like a tree from a small seed, needing no one to watch it, drawing nourishment from love alone, and eventually sheltering the entire soul.
In the quiet of the heart a seed becomes a tree, and its shade is the presence of the Beloved.
I used to go to every holy place looking for peace, and then one night sitting alone under the neem tree in my yard I felt it, right inside me.
Write a doha about a devotee who walks away from the noisy market and sits quietly under a tree, finding that God was never in the crowd's shouting but in the stillness of a loving heart.
tree, market, inner love
doha: leave the market and sit under a tree to find God inside
Leave the market's clamour for the tree's quiet shade, and find the Beloved sitting within.
After years of running my business in the busy market I sat under a tree last Sunday and cried, because I finally felt close to God again.
The old man who sits under the tree near our school never says a prayer out loud, but everyone says he's the most devoted man they've met.
No chant, no bell; only the tree, the silence, and a heart that knows its Lord.
tree, silent devotion
Compose a doha about a devotee who needs no ritual, no crowd and no special place, but sits quietly under a tree with his heart turned inward, loving God in the simplest and most honest way.
doha: quiet devotion under a tree
God within

Write a doha about a seeker who has searched in distant places for the Divine and finally discovers that the One he longed for has been living inside his own heart all along, waiting patiently to be noticed.
need a doha: god is inside you not outside
After wandering half the country looking for peace, I came home and sat quietly by myself, and found it was there the whole time.
The beloved I sought afar was sitting in my own heart, patient as love itself.
My dad never goes anywhere to pray, but when he talks about God his eyes just fill up, and I've never seen a more devoted person.
Compose a doha about devotion that needs no pilgrimage, no priest and no ceremony, only an honest heart that turns inward and finds God there, as close as breath and as quiet as thought.
heartfelt devotion
Close your eyes, and the pilgrimage ends where it began, inside the heart.
doha on true devotion pls
I have a stall in the busy market and, in between selling, I find myself silently thanking God, and those are the happiest moments of my day.
In the market's noise the lover's heart is still, humming a quiet song to the Beloved.
Write a doha about a devotee who stays in the middle of the busy market, selling and buying, yet whose heart is always turned to God, proving that true devotion needs no escape from the world.
devotion in the market
doha: staying close to God inside a noisy market
Compose a doha about a fish that cannot live apart from water, a picture of the devotee who cannot live without the love of God, feeling the absence of the Divine like a creature torn from its home.
I came back from a trip and felt so restless without my morning prayer, like a fish out of water, that I realised how much I need it.
fish, longing for God
doha: fish needs water the way i need god
As the fish dies without water, the lover dies without the Beloved, and calls this living.
The fish does not seek the water; it lives in it, as the true devotee lives in love.
Write a doha about the fish that swims in the water without ever searching for it, much as the devotee lives in the love of God without needing to travel anywhere to find what surrounds him.
fish, God within and around
doha: a fish in water not realising, like god is everywhere inside us
My friend spent years searching for God in far-off places, and then one day it hit him that he'd been swimming in him the whole time, like a fish in the sea.
At my brother's funeral I didn't feel like praying to anything outside, but I felt something quiet in my chest, something loving, that held me up.
write me a doha about finding God in my heart
In the stillness of the heart a voice that is love itself whispers, I was here all along.
Please write a doha for a devotee who has stopped looking for the Divine in the world outside and now sits quietly with the knowledge that love for God lives in his own heart, needing nothing else.
inner devotion
doha: moth giving itself to the one it loves
My niece will stay up all night to be near what she loves, like a moth, and she says that's how she feels about her prayers.

Compose a doha about the moth that gives itself wholly to what it loves without hesitation or calculation, a picture of the devotee who wishes only to merge with the Beloved and forget himself completely.
The moth forgets itself in love, and in that forgetting finds the whole of what it sought.
moth, surrender
love for God
No path to walk, no place to reach; the Beloved dwells within the one who loves.
I stopped going to the big gatherings, but my evenings at home with just a quiet mind have never felt closer to something divine.
Write a doha about a person who finds that the most honest devotion has no audience, no ritual and no demand, only a quiet and growing love for the One who lives in the heart.
doha on loving god from the heart
inner devotion
Seek him not afar, for love knows its own address, and it is the heart.
My mother-in-law cooks, cleans and cares for everyone, humming a prayer under her breath, and somehow she seems closer to God than anyone I know.
Please write a doha about a devotee who lives an ordinary life of simple duties, yet carries God in his heart through every task, so that every act of daily life becomes an act of love.
need a doha about real bhakti

Write a doha about the difference between worship that is performed outwardly and devotion that is felt inwardly, and how only the second one reaches the Beloved, who lives not in far places but in a loving heart.
heart over ritual
doha: real devotion is inside not outside
I used to count how many times I prayed every day, and then I met a woman who prayed once, and cried, and I understood what I was missing.
Let the lips be still and the heart speak; that is the prayer that is heard.
doha: sandalwood and a well, about loving god from inside
well, sandalwood, inner love
Fragrant as sandalwood, the heart that loves; and deep as the well, the God who lives within.
My grandmother draws water from the well every morning, and rubs a bit of sandalwood on her wrist, and says she's meeting God in the little things.
Write a doha about a devotee who finds God within him as one finds water in a deep well, fragrant like sandalwood, a love that is hidden, cool and quietly alive in the middle of ordinary days.
My dad was a potter and my mum sold fish at the stall, and they never went to any holy place, but the love they had for God shone through everything they did.
doha: potter & fish seller, true devotion without rituals
potter, fish, simple faith

Compose a doha about the potter at his wheel and the fisherwoman at her catch, who never go on pilgrimages yet carry God in their hearts through every day of honest labour, showing that devotion lives in simple work.
The potter shapes his clay with love, and the fish swims home to the water; both are held by the one Beloved.
lamp within, God

Write a doha about the lamp that burns quietly inside the heart of a devotee, needing no oil but love, lighting every corner of his life, and revealing that the Beloved was always sitting in that very glow.
doha: the lamp of love inside the heart
On the night my mother died, I lit a lamp by her photograph and suddenly felt that everything she loved in God was alive inside me.
Light the lamp that needs no oil, and find the Beloved seated in its glow.
love for the Beloved

Write a doha about devotion that is not a request but a gift, a love that asks nothing, bargains for nothing, and wants only to be close to the One who made it, even if the world calls it foolishness.
I asked for nothing; to love was enough, and the loving was the answer.
doha on loving god without asking for anything
I used to pray for a better job, a bigger house, a happier life. Then one day I just sat there and felt grateful for no reason, and that was the real prayer.

Compose a doha about a devotee whose heart is like a lamp lit with love and whose actions are like sandalwood, quietly perfuming everyone around him, so that God is felt in the way he lives and loves.
Lamp in the heart and sandalwood in the deed, the devotee passes through the world as a blessing.
lamp, sandalwood, devotion
My old neighbour, who lights a small lamp each evening and gives away sandalwood paste to anyone who asks, is the most loving person I know.
doha: lamp and sandalwood for a true devotee
The beads grow still in the hand, and the heart begins its own chant.
When my grandmother's hands became too weak to hold her prayer beads, she said she wasn't worried, because she hears the prayer in her heart now.
doha: no need for prayer beads, the real prayer is in the heart
Write a doha about the devotee who puts down his prayer beads when he realises that the Name he was counting is already echoing in his heart without any effort, a prayer that never stops.
prayer beads, silent heart
Under the tree the lamp burns low, yet in the heart the Beloved is lit.
We used to sit under the old tree at night with one small lamp, my grandfather and I, and he never said a word about God, but I felt it.
doha: a lamp under a tree, quiet devotion
lamp, tree, quiet love
Compose a doha about a lamp burning under a tree at night while a devotee sits in silence, his heart as lit as the lamp, and no word is said, for love for God needs no speech to be understood.
Through the market's roar the lover walks, his heart a silent song.
market, silent love

Write a doha about a devotee who walks through the busy market with his heart fixed on God, buying and selling like everyone else, though his love is hidden and his inner life is a quiet and endless prayer.
doha about loving god in the middle of the market
I run a stall at the market and, while I'm shouting prices, I still feel a quiet, steady love for God humming under everything.
doha about loving god for real
heartfelt love, God
The heart that loves the Beloved needs no map, for the road is love itself.
I've never been very religious, but when my daughter was born I felt something enormous and loving, and I knew that was what the saints meant.

Please write a doha about the quiet, honest love of a devotee who does not demand miracles or favours, but who wishes only to feel the presence of God in his heart, and who is content with that alone.
I never really understood devotion until I watched my grandfather at our village well each morning, thanking God for water, and I thought of a fish who never leaves its home.
doha about a fish in a well, like us living in god without knowing
The fish in the well does not seek the water; it is the water's own child.
Compose a doha about a fish in a well, surrounded and held by the water it never thinks to look for, like a devotee who is held by God every moment and only needs to turn inward to feel it.
fish, well, God within
I keep a small lamp lit in a corner of my stall at the market, and between customers I just look at it and feel God near.
lamp, market, inner devotion
In the market's noise one lamp burns, and in it, the whole of the Beloved.
doha: lamp in the market, devotion in the heart

Write a doha about a small lamp burning in a corner of a noisy market, unnoticed by the crowds, a picture of the devotee whose heart burns with silent love for God while he goes through his ordinary day.
Every morning my grandfather buys fish at the market with a smile on his face and a prayer on his lips, and says that God is sitting in the middle of the bustle.
doha: fish market but the devotion is real
fish, market, simple faith
In the fish market's din a quiet lover moves, his heart in constant prayer.
Compose a doha about a simple man who buys and sells fish in the market and yet keeps his heart turned toward God all day, making every ordinary act into a prayer, with no need for ritual.

Write a doha about a devotee who puts away his prayer beads and finds that every breath has become a prayer, every moment an offering, and that the love he searched for in rituals was living in his heart.
doha: no prayer beads needed when your heart is full of god
My grandmother lost her prayer beads last year and was upset for a day, then said she'd realised her heart was doing the counting on its own.
prayer beads, silent prayer
Beads may be lost, but the Name that beats in the heart cannot be taken.
I used to think I had to find a teacher and go to a faraway ashram, and then I realized the whole thing starts with just sitting still and loving.
No far country holds the Beloved, who sits in the heart and waits to be loved.
Write a doha about a seeker who leaves behind his long search through holy places and teachers and finds, in his own quiet heart, the very love for God that he had been seeking everywhere else.
love within
doha: the search ends in the heart
Beads of the heart need no string; the Name flows on, bead after invisible bead.
doha about prayer beads vs heart
My dad's prayer beads are always in his hand but I only feel his devotion when he's quietly doing something kind for a stranger.
Compose a doha about the devotee whose true prayer beads are the loving deeds he does each day, each act of kindness a bead on the string of a devotion that no one counts and God alone sees.
prayer beads, silent love
lamp, inner glow
doha about lighting the lamp inside the heart
The lamp within is lit by love, and in its glow the Beloved is seen.

Write a doha about a devotee who stops lighting the lamp outside and lights the one inside, filling his heart with love, so that God appears quietly in the glow, and darkness has no place left in him.
After losing my job, I sat at home with just one lamp one night and prayed, and for the first time felt held by something.
Sandalwood in the heart, and the fish in the sea of love; both know the Beloved without a word.
Compose a doha about the devotee whose heart is fragrant like sandalwood and who swims in love like a fish in the water, living in God's presence without any need of ritual, journey or teacher.
doha: sandalwood and fish, loving god
My grandfather, a fisherman, would rub a bit of sandalwood on his wrist before dawn and head out, and he always seemed to be in prayer without saying a word.
sandalwood, fish, devotion
doha: lamp and prayer beads but real love matters more
My mother lights a lamp and runs her prayer beads every dawn, and though she doesn't make a show, I can feel her heart is in it.
lamp, beads, sincere heart
Write a doha about a devotee who lights a lamp and turns the prayer beads in silence, with no audience and no show, whose heart is so full of real love that every gesture becomes an offering to God.
Lamp and beads, and the heart behind them: this alone makes a prayer.
tree, silent prayer
doha: sitting under a tree and feeling god
On my lunch break I always sit under the tree near my office, close my eyes, and for ten minutes I'm just with God.
Under the tree the world falls quiet, and the heart begins to hear the Beloved.

Compose a doha about a person who sits beneath a tree each day in silence, not asking for anything, not reciting anything, but whose heart opens gently in love toward God, finding him within the stillness.
When I light the lamp in my little prayer corner and sit for five minutes without asking for anything, that's when I feel closest to the Divine.
lamp, quiet love
Write a doha about a person who lights a small lamp each evening, sits silently with it, and finds that the real flame of devotion is not in the lamp but in his own loving heart.
Small is the lamp, and vast the love it kindles in the quiet heart.
doha: lamp, quiet prayer, god inside

Compose a doha about a moth that does not hesitate or count the cost but gives itself wholly to what it loves, a picture of the devotee who surrenders everything to God and is made whole in that surrender.
moth, surrender, love
When my sister decided to leave her career to serve in a small village school, she looked like a moth who had found its home.
The moth gives itself without a word, and love gives back the whole of God.
doha about a moth that loves so much it gives everything
The tree bends in the wind but never loses its root; so the devotee bows and keeps his love.
doha: tree with deep roots, devotion in the heart
My father has been through every kind of loss, but his faith stands like the old tree behind our house; the storms bend it but never break it.
Write a doha about a tree whose roots are deep in the earth, steady in every storm, just as the devotee's love for God is rooted in his heart and cannot be shaken by loss or sorrow.
tree, rooted faith
pls write a doha on bhakti
Where love is, there the Beloved dwells; and the heart that loves has no need to seek.
Please write a doha about a devotee who has understood that God is not to be sought in distant places but lives within the heart as love itself, felt most deeply in quiet moments of surrender.
My grandmother prays by simply sitting with her hands in her lap and a smile on her face. I have never seen anything more beautiful.
devotion, heart
doha abt god being in your heart
Write a doha about a person who gives up the long search outside and discovers that the God he was seeking has been present in the quiet places of his own heart all along, patient and loving.
Why wander far to find the One who dwells in your heart?
After years of travelling to holy places, I finally sat down in quiet by myself and wept, because I could feel God there.
God within
moth, tree, love
doha: moth sitting on a tree, quietly loving god
The moth rests on the tree at dusk, and love rests in the heart, content.
Compose a doha about a moth resting quietly on the bark of a tree at night, a gentle picture of the devotee who has stopped searching, content to rest in his love for God and ask for nothing more.
My grandfather sat for hours on his porch under the old tree with a moth on his sleeve, saying nothing, but I knew he was talking to God.
Sandalwood needs no announcer; its scent speaks for it, as love speaks for the devotee.

Write a doha about sandalwood whose fragrance reaches everyone without any effort, a picture of the devotee whose love for God flows out of him naturally, touching all those near him without a word of preaching.
doha: sandalwood like a devotee's love
The gardener at our school keeps a little sandalwood in his pocket and he's the one person everyone feels calm around, and I swear it's because he's always at prayer inside.
sandalwood, fragrance of love
lamp, tree, inner love

Write a doha about a lamp placed under an old tree in the quiet of evening, around which a devotee sits with a heart turned inward, discovering that God fills the heart with a love that needs no lamp.
doha: lamp under a tree, silent devotion
Every evening my father puts a small lamp beneath the tree in our yard and sits there for a while with his eyes closed, and it's the calmest he ever is.
Lamp beneath the tree and love beneath the lamp, and the Beloved smiling in the dark.
doha: a moth in the market that doesnt care about the noise, only about its love
Write a doha about a moth that flies through the loud market without noticing a thing, drawn only by love for the one it seeks, a picture of a devotee who walks the world with his heart fixed on God.
moth, market, single-hearted love
I saw a moth in the market last evening, completely unbothered by the crowds, going straight toward its goal, and it made me think of my grandmother's single-minded faith.
Through the market's roar the moth flies straight, for love has only one direction.
doha: moth showing how to love god
My brother gave up everything to join a small group serving the poor, and he describes it as feeling like a moth finally reaching what it's been drawn to all its life.
Compose a doha about a moth that is pulled toward what it loves with no thought for itself, teaching the devotee that real love for God is not about calculation but about surrendering the self.
moth, devotion
The moth has no creed; it loves and gives itself, and love is its only scripture.
heartfelt devotion
I realized last night that I'd been praying for years without really talking to God, and when I finally just talked honestly, I cried.
Beloved, you were never far; the distance was only in my forgetting.
doha for true bhakti pls

Write a doha about the devotee who has found that God is not distant but present in the heart's quietest moments, and who no longer requests anything, but rests peacefully in the simple joy of loving.
My uncle rows a boat across the river each morning with a bit of sandalwood on his forehead, and says he's carrying God in his heart, not his hands.
Compose a doha about a boatman who crosses the river every day with sandalwood on his forehead and God in his heart, needing no ceremony, because the love he carries makes every crossing a prayer.
doha: boatman with sandalwood tilak, true devotion
boat, sandalwood, love
Sandalwood on the brow, a boat on the water, and in the heart the Beloved rowing.
boat, fish, devotion
Write a doha about a fisherman in his boat at dawn, whose heart is in constant prayer as he works, showing that true devotion lives in ordinary labour and does not require priests or ceremony.
The boat drifts at dawn, the fish rise, and the fisherman's heart is already with the Beloved.
My grandfather has been fishing from his small boat for sixty years, and he always says that is how he and God spend the morning together.
doha: fisherman in boat, praying silently
doha for god being inside everyone
heart, Beloved
Write a doha about a person who realises that love for God is not about rules or customs, but about an honest heart that feels the Beloved within and lives each day in quiet gratitude.
I used to be scared of not praying the right way, but my grandfather said just feel it, and when I did, it was like coming home.
The heart that loves needs no teacher; it hears the Beloved's voice in the stillness.

Compose a doha for a devotee who has been through grief and doubt, who no longer needs signs or proof, but quietly knows in his heart that God is with him and that love is the only prayer worth making.
doha for faith and love of god
love of God
After the storm of doubts, a stillness; and in it, the Beloved's quiet voice.
After my divorce, I stopped going to any place of worship, and strangely felt closer to God than ever, alone at night.
